lines.en: And so another day comes to an end with absolutely nothing happening.
It’s almost as if becoming a teacher isn’t really as exciting as most people make it out to be.
Granted, I’m no stranger when it comes to traversing paths that most would find impassable.
Or at least I think that's the case.
I’m not the best when it comes to figuring out how the people around me feel but, then again, that’s something I’ve willed myself into doing simply because I like walking alone a little better.
I guess what I’m trying to get at here is that some days are good.
And others?
Well-
Saying they don’t matter is the nice way of putting it.
Today is one of those days- where I’m acutely aware of my state of being and how remarkably pointless it is from the perspective of some other person behind some other desk.
But, at least there’s only one more day of this until the weekly cycle of self-induced apathy and student-induced orgasms starts over.
Thankfully, this weekend comes fully equipped with yet another get together that I’m positive won’t result in any sort of drama or rivalry between classmates.
After all, nothing bad ever happens as a result of those.
And nothing bad ever happens on Christmas.
So, all things considered, I think I can count on making some memories that may or may not crush and/or consume the ones this mind used to hold.
And, even more things considered-
I wonder how much longer I can keep this up for.
Welcome to the second Lessons in Love special Christmas update!
The next twenty-something events will play in succession.
Now, I know what you’re thinking.
Why is this chain of events starting on a Thursday? And why is it starting in an office completely devoid of all traces of Christmas spirit?
Well, unfortunately, I don’t have an answer for you.
But, you see- sometimes, it’s the average days that don’t carry any sort of weight that wind up completely changing everything we know when we look back on them.
And hey, maybe this random Thursday will be one of those days.
Or maybe I’m just bullshitting you and this really won’t matter at all when everything is said and done.
I guess we never really know until things are said and done, though, huh?
Anyway, I’ll leave you alone for now.
Please cherish this Christmas- for you never know how many of them you have left.
While I nodded, nearly napping, suddenly there came a tapping.
: Come in.
: Pardon the intrusion.
: Woah. Hey.
: Can’t say I expected to see you today.
: Please hold your applause. I’m not returning to school until this coming Monday. I just came by to check on my office plants.
: Oh, and to do this.
: I am terribly sorry for the commotion I must have caused during your strange, winter beach trip.
: I can’t imagine you dwelled too much on it seeing as you made no attempt to contact neither myself nor my significant other during my stay in the hospital-
: But I don’t blame you at all on account of the position my actions must have put you in.
: It was a mistake. A bad one.
: And if there is anything I can do to prevent it from having a long-lasting effect on our friendship, please let me know.
: So it is a friendship after all.
: Well, yes. I thought that was obvious.
: You don’t have to apologize, Wakana. It’s fine.
: No, it’s not fine. And I do have to apologize.
: Even if you don’t personally care, I’m sure some of your students may have been quite frightened by the event.
: I should never have placed anyone in that position, and not apologizing for it would weigh on me greater than the bulk of life itself.
: Can you stop assuming I don’t personally care just because I didn’t go out of my way to contact you?
: I’d be willing to accept Miyamura as a token of your apology.
: I’m serious. What would I have even said if I did contact you?
: Hello, Wakana. Glad to hear you’re...still alive?
: It’s not the most eloquent way of wording it, but you have experience in writing, so I’m sure you’d figure something out.
: I won’t be petty about it, though. It’s fine.
: You seemed pretty petty just a few seconds ago.
: Yeah, well, I want to fucking die. Not literally, though.
: Osako has asked that I add that clause whenever I utter those words as she’s still understandably shaken up over the whole thing.
: Would you mind...explaining what happened, maybe? I still don’t really understand what went down.
: I didn’t even know you were on drugs until I woke up and heard that you were rushed to the hospital.
: I’m not on drugs- and this may be hard to believe given the type of person that I’ve painted myself to be, but I wasn’t trying to kill myself either.
: I just took a little too much of my pain medication and it caused my body to temporarily shut down.
: That sounds like more than just a “little too much.”
: Yeah, I'm aware. And I’ve spent essentially every conscious minute since then apologizing for it.
: If I could go back and just deal with it, I would. But that ship has sailed and carried us off to the middle of nowhere, and now I just want to go home.
: I have a problem. It is no fault of yours, nor is it any fault of Osako’s, but I need you to understand that it is not something I wanted or asked for.
: Hey, I was just being a little sarcastic. You don’t have to freak out.
: I’m not-
: Ugh.
: And now the lack of medication is causing me to speak out of turn.
: There’s truly no winning in this world, is there?
: Nope, but there’s certainly losing. And you came pretty damn close to doing that at the beach.
: So just...be good or whatever and don’t almost kill yourself again and I’m sure everything will be just fine.
: ...Yeah.
: You know, if you didn’t spend virtually all of your free time committing heinous acts on high school girls, you might actually be a decent person.
: And if you didn’t spend all of your free time binding and gagging my karate instructor, you might find that you’re into the same sort of stuff that I am.
: Which isn’t me admitting anything, by the way.
: I’m sure.
: Ahem...
: Oh, look. A conveniently timed knock that prevents this conversation from going somewhere unfavorable.
: Yo, let me in! I have to tell you about a thing!
: Unless you’re helping some student with her problems or something! If that’s the case, I’m sorry and I will wait!
: It’s fine. You can come in.
: What, am I not cool enough to get invited to your secret teacher meetings or something?
: Sorry, but I think Wakana coming back means that you’re officially unemployed again.
: What?! She’s back?! But I had a whole ‘nother month of cool shit planned!
: Ahh. You must be the one who replaced me, then.
: Imani Imai. You’re...Wakana Watabe, right?
: Yes, but...what are we doing with our hands, exactly?
: Bonding. We’re friends now.
: We are?
: Yeah. All three of us are. We’re like those three amigos or whatever. Just instead of fighting people with swords and stuff, we fight them with information.
: I think you're thinking of the three musketeers.
: I take it you two have already gotten acquainted, then?
: She just kind of showed up while Noriko was pouring her heart out to me in school the other day.
: Noriko?
: The anarchist girl that you pawned off on me.
: Oh.
: She’s still fawning over you to that extent? I had assumed that was just a one time thing.
: She’s gotten...better.
: You two married yet? Because I don’t remember getting a wedding invite.
: We are not, no. Nor are we going to be any time soon.
: Are you going to come too? You seem pretty close to this guy since you came to his office before even dropping by your classroom.
: Wait, did you really come straight to my-
: Miss...Imai, would you be willing to fill me in on what you’ve been teaching my class during my leave of absence?
: Or just ignore me. That’s fine.
: You can call me Imani, it’s cool. And they’re doing great, actually.
: I will admit that I may have veered a little far off the curriculum, but that’s kinda just how I do stuff.
: So my bad if everyone is suddenly like, really knowledgeable about the Crusades and praying mantises and shit.
: Those...are certainly strange topics to specialize in.
: You all good now, Wakana? You were in the hospital, right?
: Well enough to return to school, I suppose.
: Which means that, come Monday, you’ll likely be moved to a temporary position or something along those lines.
: You think?
: Quite often. Though, I can’t say the thoughts are always colorful or jubilant.
: And what do you think, Sensei? Where will I wind up?
: New school nurse? Vice principal? Janitor?
: For your own safety, I hope you don’t wind up as the janitor.
: Our school has a strange history of losing members of the custodial staff to freak accidents or, on some occasions, manslaughter.
: Well, damn. I thought Japanese schools were supposed to be safe. I didn’t realize I was walking into some kind of murder zone when I took this job.
: Where are you from, if you don’t mind me asking?
: Switzerland.
: I see.
: Wales.
: Alabama.
: Okay, fine. I moved here from Ghana right before the city was closed off.
: I just thought it would be funny to name all of the whitest places I could think of since you don’t really have many teachers that look like me here.
: And by many I mean literally none. It’s just me.
: Is that something you’re not comfortable with?
: Oh, no. I’m totally cool with it. Just an awkward attempt at humor, I guess. I don’t know.
: Even though I’ve been here for a few years now, I still don’t really have any friends. And I just thought it’d be kinda cool if like, you know, all three of us could hang out sometime or something.
: But if you’d rather keep it professional or whatever, that’s fine too. You can just think I’m weird and I’ll go crawl in a hole and die.
: Hm.
: I mean...I’m fine with hanging out sometimes. Wakana is the one who’ll likely need convincing.
: Wakanaaaaaaa.
: Wakanaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.
: Wakana Wakana Wakanaaaaaa.
: What are you doing?
: Will you pleeeeeease be my friend?
: I don’t think that sort of thing will work on-
: Sure.
: Oh.
: Hell yeah! Teacher pals! Knowledge partners! Education...compadres!
: Why do you think I’m so against the idea of socializing with my peers?
: Because you spend roughly half of every day either talking about how you want to die or complaining about your students.
: But when do I ever complain about people who aren’t students?
: You complain about me literally all the time.
: And yet I came here before even watering my plants.
: Wait, are you two fucking?
: Uhh...what?
: Oh my God! Is that what you were about to do before I knocked on the door?! Am I interrupting a sweet reunion bang sesh right now?!
: Sorry. I’ll close my eyes. I’m sure it must have been hard after all of that time apart. Just forget I’m even here.
: Have at thee!
: Welp, you heard her Wakana. Let’s commence with our planned sexual intercourse now.
: Open your eyes. I’m dating a woman.
: Oh, shit.
: And she’s okay with you banging your male coworker?
: Is there something else you need, Imani?
: Maybe some ear plugs so I don’t hear anything when you two start going at it?
: Leaving the office would also suffice, you know.
: Please don’t insinuate that any of what she’s saying bears any ounce of truth whatsoever.
: I can’t leave. What if someone saw me come in here after you two and they think I’m a part of this secret tryst?
: Wouldn’t leaving before us sort of quell that notion?
: Nooooo because then they’ll think I’m bad at stuff and that I couldn’t keep up with all of the action! I’m a part of this now!
: Well, either we have a threesome or we all leave this office together and just...go home since it’s already well past school hours.
: Hmmmmmmmmmm...
: I don’t believe Osako would take kindly to the idea of a threesome she isn’t involved in.
: Would she...take kindly to the idea of one she is involved in?
: Maybe? I’ve never asked.
: Wait! But then what will happen to me?! Three plus one does not equal three! I know this because I am a teacher!
: In lieu of any sexual activities, I propose that the three of us simply leave here together and...find something else to do if we’re not yet done with this...reunion-slash-introduction.
: Does that work for you?
: I mean...I was kind of planning on just going home, but if you really want to keep hanging out, I guess I can do that instead.
: How kind of you, making time for your recently near-departed friend.
: I’m game! Hanging out normally sounds a lot less...sticky than a threesome, too.
: My only condition is that any and all discussions about threesomes cease immediately, as I was already intending to visit Osako at the maid cafe.
: I’ve just added the two of you to the plan as well because...friendship.
: I’m gonna cry. It’s been years since I’ve gone out with coworkers.
: If you cry, I’m rescinding your invitation and cancelling our friendship indefinitely.
: I’ll...*sniff*
: I’ll do my best...
Somehow or another, I wind up getting dragged into a get together with Wakana and Imani.
Well, I guess dragged isn’t really an accurate term since I’m not really against the idea of spending time with the two of them.
I would have just much preferred the original idea since the new one doesn’t contain group sex.
But alas, those are thoughts I can not allow myself to be burdened with in the presence of someone who could eliminate me at the drop of a hat.
Actually, now that she’s in my mind- I wonder how Osako’s doing with the whole Wakana situation.
I’d decided to stay out of her affairs so she could have time to figure things out with Wakana, but...
Now that Wakana is doing, at least on a surface level, much better...I wonder if any of those worries I was, well, worried about have vanished.
But just thinking that won’t help.
In fact, thinking rarely ever does anything to begin with.
I’ll just continue to go with the flow, hang out with a small group of coworkers like a normal functioning adult, and see how things play out from here.
Without any interference from me.
Wakana’s affection has increased to [wakana_love]!
Imani’s affection has increased to [imani_love]!
